findings.issue: Trivy vulnerability scanner uses @master mutable tag — not pinned to a specific SHA or semver
findings.impact: Supply chain risk: a compromised or updated @master could introduce malicious code into CI pipeline without review
findings.fix: Pin trivy-action to a specific SHA (e.g., aquasecurity/trivy-action@595be6a...) or semver tag (e.g., @v0.28.0)

findings.issue: Trivy action also uses @master tag in build-push.yml — same supply chain issue
findings.impact: Supply chain risk across two CI workflows using unpinned mutable reference
findings.fix: Pin trivy-action to a specific SHA in build-push.yml as well

findings.issue: pnpm audit threshold set to --audit-level=moderate — only blocks moderate+ severity; high/critical advisories pass if below moderate threshold
findings.impact: High-severity dependency vulnerabilities may not block CI; false sense of security from audit check
findings.fix: Set --audit-level=high to at minimum block high-severity vulnerabilities; consider blocking at critical level

findings.issue: wget installed in production Docker image — unnecessary package increases runtime attack surface
findings.impact: Extra package in production container provides additional attack vector for RCE exploits
findings.fix: Remove wget from production Dockerfile; use curl or HEALTHCHECK built-in instead

findings.issue: Docker multi-stage builds use npm ci and then discard devDependencies, but pnpm store is not cleaned — final image may contain package manager artifacts
findings.impact: Unnecessary layer bloat increases image size and attack surface
findings.fix: Add pnpm store prune and .pnpm-store directory cleanup in final stage

findings.issue: No Dependabot or Renovate configuration for automated dependency updates — .github/dependabot.yml does not exist
findings.impact: Dependency vulnerabilities may go unnoticed until manually discovered; no automated PRs for security patches
findings.fix: Create .github/dependabot.yml with weekly checks for npm, GitHub Actions, and Docker dependencies

findings.issue: Dockerfile has HEALTHCHECK (good) but no USER directive — containers run as root by default
findings.impact: If container is compromised, attacker has root access inside the container
findings.fix: Add 'USER appuser' after installing dependencies; create appuser in Dockerfile
